adoptionSource: operator instructions 2026-10-18 (documentation-and-publication phase authorization; separate accounting granted)
amendmentPolicy: material scope/acceptance changes require explicit operator version-adoption recorded as a NEW canonical decision with --supersedes; suggestions never auto-enter task totals or later phases

digestNormalization.rationale: contractDigest excluded to avoid self-referential recursion; planRevision excluded because the canonical Decision binds plan_revision at record time — the adoption writer stamps both fields AFTER digest computation; the read-only checker re-computes with this identical normalization and compares against the canonical decision payload
digestNormalization.stalenessRule: STALE iff the latest non-superseded adoption decision for this contract path carries a digest != recomputed digest, or the adoption decision has been superseded by a newer adoption for the same path. planRevision is traceability metadata, not an equality gate.

evidenceInvalidation: keyed by source digest / plan revision / fixture identity; only affected evidence invalidated; history preserved; no full-repo re-review loops; gates that passed and were not invalidated are not re-run
functionalScope: Publish the qualified candidate (commits ebc8f687 + 9a7c4bbf on codex/kbd-phase-readiness) as the next unused versioned release: (1) documentation across README, KBD docs, CHANGELOG, Docusaurus site covering planning contract, readiness gate, execution flow, evidence-bound closure, missing-accounting BLOCKED behavior, budgets, installation, and a practical example, with explicit disclosure of shell-layer enforcement, bypassable paths, self-reported accounting, and installed-demonstration limits; (2) version selection from existing tags/metadata/conventions, release notes linking docs/releases/1.12.2-candidate-qualification.md (kept intact); (3) required release-policy checks and docs/site build, distribution regeneration if needed, confirming the release includes the qualified evaluator and gate; (4) scoped commits only, branch push, release PR, in-scope CI failure resolution only; (5) merge only when required checks/approvals pass, publish version + Docusaurus via existing configured workflow, verify tag/artifact identity, documentation URL, installation instructions; (6) GitHub issue reconciliation — close only criteria-met issues, keep #184/#185 open with release link and remaining scope.
exclusions: no force-push, no branch-protection bypass, no overwriting a published version
no unrelated working-tree changes in commits
no new credentials, permissions, or paid resources without operator approval
no successor hardening, mini-pack work, phase-exit integration, or additional features
no rerunning unrelated behavioral suites for prose/version-metadata-only changes
no hosted CI as acceptance evidence beyond what the repository's release policy requires

releaseClaim.userOperation: operator installs the published skill-pack version, reads the published documentation (contract, gate, execution flow, closure, budgets, installation, example, limitations), and reconciles GitHub issues against what shipped
supportedEnvironments: GitHub hosting for PR/release (pre-authorized for this phase)
releaseClaim.currentCapabilities: candidate ebc8f687+9a7c4bbf is qualified for controlled use per docs/releases/1.12.2-candidate-qualification.md; this phase publishes it with documentation
explicitUnknowns: exact required-CI set on the release PR (discovered at PR time; resolved only in-scope)
whether Docusaurus deployment needs permissions beyond the existing configured workflow (stop for approval if so)

requiredSafetyChecks: canonical writer only for adoption/closure/blocker records
scoped commits only; unrelated dirty paths preserved

resilienceScope.policy: adopted requirements never defer by budget overflow (exhaustion => checkpoint+BLOCKED, report 'candidate qualified; publication blocked' with the exact unfinished action)
deferredOptional: Docusaurus theme/layout redesign beyond content updates

workerRoutes.billing: operator-confirmed Kimi coding subscription endpoint, Extra Usage disabled

consumedAtAuthoring.note: new, explicitly granted publication-phase limits; historical consumption (est. ~213 min, ~166 calls, 6/6 repairs measured) preserved separately and not reset

budgets.exhaustion: checkpoint + BLOCKED; never silent PASS; docs/state may be saved without running product tests

scenarioMatrix.name: DOCUMENTATION-COMPLETE
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: edit README.md, CHANGELOG.md, KBD guide docs, and site/docs pages; grep the committed files for required topic and disclosure markers
scenarioMatrix.oracle: every required topic marker present in committed docs (planning contract, readiness gate, execution flow, evidence-bound closure, missing-accounting BLOCKED behavior, budgets, installation, practical example) AND every required disclosure marker present (shell-layer enforcement, bypassable paths, self-reported accounting, installed-demonstration limits); no claim of automatic enforcement in every harness
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: grep for a marker string that was deliberately NOT written returns no match (proves the grep oracle is live)
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: the repository's own README/docs/site files at this branch
scenarioMatrix.evidence: changed file paths + grep outputs per marker

scenarioMatrix.name: VERSION-SELECTED-UNUSED
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: git tag --list; inspect package.json + CHANGELOG conventions; select next unused version; bump package.json; create docs/releases/<new>/ notes linking the 1.12.2 candidate qualification note
scenarioMatrix.oracle: selected version absent from git tag --list before tagging; package.json version equals selection; CHANGELOG gains the version section; new release-notes file links docs/releases/1.12.2-candidate-qualification.md; the qualification note itself is byte-identical to its pre-phase content
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: selecting the already-published v1.12.2 is rejected by the tag-collision check (proves the unused-version oracle is live)
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: existing tags v1.12.2, v1.10.0, v1.8.0... as the collision baseline
scenarioMatrix.evidence: git tag output, package.json diff, release notes path

scenarioMatrix.name: RELEASE-CHECKS-PASS
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: run the repository's required release checks (check:release-version, check:distribution, docs build) and confirm the packaged evaluator carries the qualified behavior
scenarioMatrix.oracle: each required check exits 0; dist payloads contain kbd-phase-close-eval.sh with the budget-consumption-missing BLOCKED marker; docs/site build succeeds
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: marker grep against a file known not to contain it returns nothing (proves the marker oracle is live); a distribution left stale fails --check
scenarioMatrix.evidence: command argv + exit codes + marker grep output

scenarioMatrix.name: DELIVERY-PR-OPEN
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: commit only in-scope changes; push codex/kbd-phase-readiness; open the release PR with gh; inspect required checks
scenarioMatrix.oracle: git show --stat of each new commit touches only in-scope paths; unrelated pre-existing dirty paths remain uncommitted; gh pr view returns the PR URL; required-check list recorded
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: an unrelated dirty path staged by mistake is caught by git status review before commit and excluded
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: pre-existing unrelated working-tree dirt (~164 typed-runtime paths, runtime projections) as the exclusion baseline
scenarioMatrix.evidence: commit hashes + gh pr view output + CI check list

scenarioMatrix.name: PUBLISHED-AND-VERIFIED
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: merge after required checks/approvals; publish the versioned tag/release and Docusaurus via the existing configured workflow; verify tag/artifact identity, documentation URL, and installation instructions
scenarioMatrix.oracle: remote tag for the selected version exists and points at the merged release commit; release notes link the qualification note; documentation URL returns the updated content; installation instructions in the published docs match the published artifact
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: remote history is fast-forward only (no force-push); a version collision on tag creation fails instead of overwriting
scenarioMatrix.evidence: git ls-remote / gh release view output, docs URL fetch, install command from published docs

scenarioMatrix.name: ISSUES-RECONCILED
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: gh issue view/close/comment for affected issues against actual shipped scope
scenarioMatrix.oracle: #186 closed only if its acceptance criteria are met by the release, with a comment linking the release; #184 and #185 remain open, each with a comment linking the release and stating the remaining scope; no issue closed by discarding or redefining requirements
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: before closing any issue, its acceptance criteria are quoted in the reconciliation record; an unmet criterion blocks closure
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: issues #184, #185, #186 current bodies and acceptance criteria
scenarioMatrix.evidence: gh issue view state before/after + comment URLs

expectedEffects: dist payloads carry the qualified evaluator
phase closure evidence with budgetConsumption recorded via kbd-phase-close-eval.sh

stopConditions: budgets exhausted => checkpoint+BLOCKED with 'candidate qualified; publication blocked' report
frozen criteria met => terminate, no invented follow-up work
